semantic_atoms.claim: With gespraech.aktiv enabled, every non-empty local VoiceLite speech_end transcript can start a Realtime conversation; the live path explicitly does not require or call the wake-word matcher.

The triggering local speech_end result and transcript cause realtime_gespraech.fuehren_gespraech() to run, but the inspected call passes API/config/Claude-session/room-session context only. It does not pass a dedicated activation_event_id, local audio-segment identity, transcript digest/generation or other replay-stable causal identity for the exact utterance that opened this Realtime invocation.

The live activation path says no wake word is required, but after a conversation the room pulse still reports waiting for 'Hey FranKenstein'. Historical/wake-word helper semantics therefore coexist with the current reactive activation law and must not be treated as current activation provenance.
The immediate dispatch result is returned to Realtime as function_call_output carrying the original call_id. This is an explicit protocol-level result binding for the immediate tool result.

Later background completion is logged with auftrag_id, then reintroduced to the Realtime conversation as a new role=user input_text message followed by response creation. The conversation item is not function_call_output and carries neither the original call_id nor auftrag_id in the injected text/item. Therefore protocol-level causal attribution of the asynchronous completion to the original function call is not preserved in the conversation path.

task_completion outcome logging preserves auftrag_id as best-effort telemetry, but a log-side identifier is not itself a typed conversation/result join and cannot mint exact result re-entry provenance for the model response.

VoiceActivationBinding_v1.purpose: Bind local reactive speech activation to the exact Realtime invocation without timestamp/session heuristics.

VoiceAsyncReturnBinding_v1.purpose: Preserve exact lineage from original Realtime function call through asynchronous background work to later spoken result re-entry.

contradictions_preserved: Historical/module wake-word wording remains present while the current live listener intentionally starts on any non-empty speech_end when enabled.
Immediate Realtime tool result has a clean call_id join, while later asynchronous completion re-entry is converted into an unbound user-role text item.
The async completion log knows auftrag_id, but the model-facing conversation item does not carry that exact task identity.
counterhypotheses: Conversation chronology may be sufficient for human-legible reporting in a single-task session, but it is not a deterministic causal identity and can fail under overlapping background tasks or reordered completions.
An external/private runtime component may already map local activation or background completion to exact IDs outside the inspected donor repository; that remains UNKNOWN rather than denied.

required_changes: Mint VoiceActivationBinding/v1 before entering the Realtime session and pass its identity into the session object/log/response provenance.
Remove or mark historical wake-word status text so it cannot be mistaken for current activation law.
Persist original call_id alongside task/auftrag_id at async dispatch; on completion create a typed VoiceAsyncReturnBinding/v1 before model re-entry.

Do not represent system-generated background completion as if it were human-originated speech; preserve a distinct internal/result provenance channel even if the provider conversation API ultimately requires a message item.
Falsify cross-wiring with two overlapping background calls completing in reverse order.

sparse_world_substrate_effect: NO_WORLD_FACT_PROMOTION. Activation and async-return bindings are provenance/interconnect identities only. Neither local STT text nor model-generated reporting mints canonical observation or world transition truth.
next_exact_gate: Triggerword-4 build/verification lane: implement source-bound VoiceActivationBinding/v1 and VoiceAsyncReturnBinding/v1, then run a non-provider deterministic two-overlapping-background-completion reverse-order regression plus activation replay/provenance tests before any runtime promotion.
